title: The effect of pranic healing based on Rogers' therapeutic touch on cardiorespiratory indices and pain during venipuncture in pediatrics: A randomized clinical trial.
note: 46 children randomized to Rogers-based Pranic Healing or usual care during venipuncture, five minutes before/during/after; selected pain/vital signs favored intervention. Abstract identifies Rogers Therapeutic Touch theory, not Master Choa Kok Sui lineage. Keep distinct until Methods/training confirm identity; masking description needs verification.

title: A systematic review of the quality of research on hands-on and distance healing: clinical and laboratory studies.
note: Quality review of 45 clinical/45 laboratory healing studies through 2001. Includes heterogeneous hands-on/distant modalities and major methodological problems. Use for citation chasing, not primary replication or Spiritualist-specific efficacy.

title: Physiological changes in energy healers during self-practice.
note: Named Reconnective Healers confirmed in abstract: 50 practitioners versus 31 Reiki masters and 32 controls during self-practice. HRV decreased in Reconnective group, contrary to greater relaxation; blood perfusion increased. No recipient treatment efficacy or random assignment demonstrated.

title: Group Coaching Using Energy-Based Practices for Health, Healing, and Personal Growth: Program Design and Training Outcomes.
note: Sixteen coaching students, phase-one training-curriculum evaluation. Abstract does not identify Eden specifically or give a controlled clinical outcome. Retain as educational context, without attribution to Eden efficacy.

title: Gamma radiation fluctuations during alternative healing therapy.
note: Polarity Therapy explicitly identified: 10 treatment, 10 sham and 10 standing-observer volunteers, gamma detector readings at four sites. Reported lower counts do not establish emitted healing energy, beneficial radiation hormesis or cancer survival. Instrument/environment controls and allocation need full-text appraisal.

title: Case Report: Dynamic Interdependencies Between Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) Practice, Urinary Interleukin-6 Levels, and Fatigue in a Breast Cancer Survivor.
note: JSJ explicitly one of multiple CAM activities in a 49-year-old breast-cancer survivor observed for 28 days. Urinary IL6/fatigue time-series associations cannot isolate JSJ or causation. Same patient/period as PMID33412954 is probable; treat as overlapping until reconciled.

title: Advancing the Quadruple Aim Through Workplace-Integrated Holistic Wellness Interventions: A Quality Improvement Evaluation.
note: JSJ explicitly among workplace wellness modalities over 11 months; independent anonymous samples 166 baseline/158 follow-up. Self-care/healing-culture scores did not significantly change. Quality-improvement evaluation cannot isolate JSJ or treat the samples as paired longitudinal individuals.

title: Dynamic Effects of CAM Techniques on Inflammation and Emotional States: An Integrative Single-Case Study on a Breast Cancer Survivor.
note: JSJ explicitly included with music, physiotherapy and energy healing in one breast-cancer survivor's 28-day time series. Cyclic mood/neopterin associations; no comparator or isolated JSJ effect. Probable overlap with PMID34149467, not independent replication.

title: Differential Effects of Ethical Education, Physical Hatha Yoga, and Mantra Meditation on Well-Being and Stress in Healthy Participants-An Experimental Single-Case Study.
note: Mantra explicitly identified: 57 randomized across baseline lengths/four eight-week packages, 42 analyzed. Ethical-education combinations had larger well-being gains; mantra-only well-being unchanged and stress direction unfavorable. Related cohort reports PMIDs36142006/35956171 must not be counted independently.

title: Embodied Cognition in Meditation, Yoga, and Ethics-An Experimental Single-Case Study on the Differential Effects of Four Mind-Body Treatments.
note: 42 completers from 57 randomized across the same four mantra/yoga/ethics packages as PMID34421729. Selected embodied-awareness measures improved; mantra-only affect least favorable. Follow-up two/twelve months; secondary report, not independent replication or energy-mechanism proof.

title: Pilot clinical trial of a clinical meditation and imagery intervention for chronic pain after spinal cord injury.
note: 24 people with spinal-cord-injury pain randomized to combined mindfulness/mantra/imagery or health education, weekly two-hour classes for four weeks. Primary pain interference improved more in control, d>1; selected secondary outcomes favored combined practice. Do not attribute package to isolated mantra efficacy.

title: Who Benefits Most? Interactions between Personality Traits and Outcomes of Four Incremental Meditation and Yoga Treatments.
note: Moderator analysis of 57 randomized participants across four eight-week mantra/yoga/ethics packages. Personality-outcome associations are exploratory; same project as PMIDs34421729/36142006. No independent replication or validated personalized treatment-selection rule established.

title: Journey into healing: the transformative experience of shamanic healing on women with temporomandibular joint disorders.
note: PMC13023138 Methods confirms practitioners trained by the Foundation for Shamanic Studies and Sandra Ingerman, supporting Core Shamanism lineage. Twenty of 23 women completed five individualized visits, including soul retrieval and integration. Randomization was to practitioners, with no untreated/sham group. Qualitative experiences are not controlled efficacy. Same cohort as PMIDs17985808/22745613; full Methods, Results and Discussion reviewed.

title: Feasibility and short-term outcomes of a shamanic treatment for temporomandibular joint disorders.
note: 23 women with TMD, five visits; random assignment was to four practitioners, not treatment versus control. Pain/function improved within cohort. Lineage and cohort connection are confirmed by Methods and citation in full companion report PMID21040886 (Foundation for Shamanic Studies/Sandra Ingerman). Do not count as an RCT efficacy comparison.

title: Shamanism as a Clinical Intervention: A Scoping Review.
note: Scoping review of heterogeneous shamanism: 16 publications, one clinical trial, case series/reports. Use for citation chasing; review counts are not independent trials and do not establish Core Shamanism lineage for every included study.

title: Shamanic Healing for Veterans with PTSD: A Case Series.
note: Six veterans in uncontrolled shamanic-healing PTSD case series; semi-structured ritual components and acceptability reported. Abstract does not identify Foundation for Shamanic Studies/Harner training. Core Shamanism attribution and controlled PTSD efficacy remain unconfirmed.

title: Antinociceptive Efficacy of Shamanic Healing for the Management of Temporomandibular Disorders: An Evidence-Based Review.
note: TMD shamanic-healing review includes three publications with matching female age range, potentially overlapping reports from one cohort. Citation chasing needed; neither three independent trials nor general Core Shamanism efficacy established.

title: Long-term outcomes of shamanic treatment for temporomandibular joint disorders.
note: Nine-month follow-up of the same 23-woman TMD phase-one cohort; improvements did not significantly change after treatment, p>.18. This is persistence within an uncontrolled cohort, not controlled efficacy. Companion Methods PMID21040886 confirms Foundation for Shamanic Studies lineage and shared participants.

title: Power animal journeying in Western psychotherapy: Applications, therapeutic safety, and future promises.
note: Fourteen therapists interviewed about power-animal guided imagery. Perceived benefits and suitability concerns described; no controlled patient outcomes or explicit Core Shamanism training lineage in abstract. Keep identity open.

title: The experiential foundations of shamanic healing.
note: Anthropological surveys and observation of more than 30 Asian shamans describe anomalous experiences and beliefs. No Core Shamanism treatment trial or objective confirmation of the belief claims.

title: Shamanism as a healing paradigm for complementary therapy.
note: Narrative discussion of shamanism, imagery and immune-system hypotheses. No original controlled treatment results; congruence with psychoneuroimmunology is an interpretation, not validation of Core Shamanism mechanisms.

title: A Farmer Becoming a Quasi-doctor: The Daegok Diary and Rural Healthcare from the 1960s to the 1980s.
note: Historical Korean diary analysis of rural healthcare and Western medicines. Discussion of shamanic-healing myths does not study Core Shamanism as an intervention.

title: What we can learn from shamanic healing: brief psychotherapy with Latino immigrant clients.
note: Psychotherapy commentary drawn from 700 Latino immigrant families and Peruvian shamanic roots. This is not the named Harner/Foundation for Shamanic Studies method and provides no controlled Core Shamanism efficacy result.

title: The vidente phenomenon in third world traditional healing: an Amazonian example.
note: Amazonian vidente title with no PubMed abstract. Cannot identify Harner/Core Shamanism lineage or extract outcomes from title; original text required.

title: Spiritual healing as a therapy for chronic pain: a randomized, clinical trial.
note: 120 chronic-pain patients in randomized face-to-face/sham and distant/no-healing comparisons, 30 minutes weekly eight weeks. No significant healing-control differences. Generic spiritual healing across organizations; Spiritualist-specific lineage unconfirmed.

title: Assessing the feasibility of a spiritual healing intervention for adults with moderate depression: A pilot randomized controlled trial.
note: 28 adults randomized to individualized spiritual healing plus usual care or usual care, depression feasibility pilot. Scores favored intervention descriptively, but sample small/no sham. Generic healer practice does not establish Spiritualist identity. Registry NCT04766242 names feasibility primary and symptom scores secondary; status stale and endpoint reporting needs reconciliation.

title: Impact of spiritual healing on moderate depression in adults: a study protocol of a pilot randomised controlled trial (RCT).
note: Protocol for 28-person generic spiritual-healing depression pilot, NCT04766242. Planned procedures/ethics are not completed results or Spiritualist efficacy. Linked results PMID39864754 must be treated as same planned study, not replication.

title: A pragmatic, three-arm randomised controlled trial of spiritual healing for asthma in primary care.
note: 88 adults with asthma randomized to five spiritual-healing sessions, actor placebo or usual care. Primary AQLQ between-group p=.57; no specific benefit demonstrated. Abstract does not confirm Spiritualist lineage; PMC listing returned no body through attempted API route.

title: A randomized controlled trial of spiritual healing in restricted neck movement.
note: 68 restricted-neck-movement volunteers randomized to three weekly approximately 30-minute spiritual-healing visits versus usual care. Selected movement/pain contrasts positive, without placebo control. Specific Spiritualist training/lineage not identified in abstract.

title: Spiritual healing in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis: an exploratory single centre, parallel-group, double-blind, three-arm, randomised, sham-controlled trial.
note: 96 women with RA randomized across active/sham/no-healing arms, eight sessions over 21 weeks and eight-week follow-up; 82 completed. DAS28 difference .62, CI .13-1.11, statistically but not clinically significant; Doppler null. Generic energy/spiritual healing does not confirm Spiritualist identity.

title: A systematic review of the quality of research on hands-on and distance healing: clinical and laboratory studies.
note: Quality review of 45 clinical/45 laboratory healing studies through 2001. Includes heterogeneous hands-on/distant modalities and major methodological problems. Use for citation chasing, not primary replication or Spiritualist-specific efficacy.

title: The efficacy of "distant healing": a systematic review of randomized trials.
note: Systematic review of 23 heterogeneous distant-healing trials, 2774 participants, through 1999. Mixed positive/null/negative results and heterogeneity precluded pooling. Review cannot assign all findings to Spiritualist healing.

title: Effectiveness of Spiritist "passe" (Spiritual healing) for anxiety levels, depression, pain, muscle tension, well-being, and physiological parameters in cardiovascular inpatients: A randomized controlled trial.
note: 41 cardiac inpatients in Spiritist passe/sham/no-intervention trial, ten minutes on three days. Named Spiritist passe is distinct from the catalogue's Spiritualist lineage. Retain cross-tradition context without relabeling as Spiritualist or discarding the actual outcomes.

title: Effect of spiritual healing on chronic idiopathic pain: a medical and psychological study.
note: 24 chronic idiopathic-pain patients randomized to spiritual healing or no active treatment. Most clinical variables unchanged; selected sleep/psychological findings reported. Half of treated participants felt relief, which is not a controlled causal effect. Spiritualist lineage not established in abstract.

title: Effectiveness of distant healing for patients with chronic fatigue syndrome: a randomised controlled partially blinded trial (EUHEALS).
note: 409 CFS patients, six-month immediate/deferred distant healing, factorial blinded/unblinded design. No significant primary mental-health or secondary physical-health benefit; expectation associated with outcomes. Healers from multiple traditions, not a confirmed isolated Spiritualist intervention.

title: Chronically ill patients treated by spiritual healing improve in quality of life: results of a randomized waiting-list controlled study.
note: 119 chronically ill patients, five-month distant healing versus waitlist. Self-reported QOL favored treatment and expectation correlated with outcome; unblinded mixed methods. Specific Spiritualist lineage not established.

title: Pranic healing: an energy-based healing practice for the contemporary nurse.
note: Narrative review introducing Pranic Healing to nursing. Arguments and selected discoveries are not original controlled clinical results.

title: Introducing the Pranic Healing system to holistic nursing practice.
note: Indexed review on introducing Pranic Healing to nursing; no PubMed abstract available. No efficacy outcomes can be extracted; use for teaching/citation context pending original text.

title: Complementary and alternative medicine: the move into mainstream health care.
note: Broad CAM policy/practice discussion mentioning Pranic Healing. Population-use statistics are not PH efficacy results.

title: Polarity addresses the "whole" in holistic.
note: Narrative Polarity process review. Describes energetic rationale and possible uses, not a completed controlled efficacy experiment.

title: Positive well-being changes associated with giving and receiving Johrei healing.
note: 236 participants rated feelings/well-being before/after giving or receiving Johrei. Receivers had greater negative-emotion reductions; both roles improved positive states. No untreated/sham comparator, so role contrast does not establish energy-specific efficacy.

title: Pranic healing.
note: Pranic Healing narrative review asserting molecular/energy effects. No original controlled sample or quantitative endpoint provided in abstract; assertion not validation.

title: Johrei, a Japanese healing technique, enhances the growth of sucrose crystals.
note: Sucrose-crystallization experiments compare Johrei-treated and untreated solutions, reporting faster growth. Nonbiological outcome does not establish patient efficacy or mechanism; sample, environmental controls and precision need full text.

title: Agnihotra in the treatment of alcoholism.
note: 18 alcoholism cases with repeated Agnihotra; abstinence reported after two weeks and 55% beyond eight weeks. Uncontrolled series, selection/other-treatment confounding and ascertainment limit causal efficacy; not a demonstrated cure.

title: Agnihotra - a useful adjunct in recovery of a resistant demotivated smack addict.
note: One poorly motivated opioid-addiction case after withdrawal, four weeks of Agnihotra and reported one-year follow-up. Uncontrolled recovery cannot establish treatment efficacy or relapse prevention.

title: Normal and diseased personal eye modeling using age-appropriate lens parameters.
note: Ocular optical modeling using lens bio-geometry. Not BioGeometry energy-healing method.

title: Comment on Some implications of the reported effects of Johrei on the viability and proliferation of cultured cancer cells in vitro.
note: Comment on Johrei cultured-cancer-cell findings, with no abstract. Commentary is not an independent experiment; obtain text for methodological criticism/citation context.

title: Effect of Spiritist "passe" (Spiritual healing) on growth of bacterial cultures.
note: Bacterial-culture study of Spiritist passe/laying on hands; Johrei appears only among background examples. No Johrei intervention tested.

title: Transmigration, liminality, and spiritualist healing.
note: Ethnographic Spiritualist church observations in New York; describes rituals and symbolic states. Named tradition present but no controlled clinical endpoint or measured therapeutic efficacy.

title: Development of dental charts according to tooth development and eruption for Turkish children and young adults.
note: Dental eruption charts using an unrelated Bengston system. No Bengston Healing Method intervention.

title: Dental age estimation standards for a Western Australian population.
note: Dental age-estimation standards use Bengston eruption classification. No healing-with-intent intervention.

title: Johrei Effects on Water: A Pilot Study by Counting Drops.
note: Four Johrei practitioners, modeled water-drop behavior versus untreated samples. Selected parameters changed for two practitioners; no patient efficacy tested. Model fit is not replication or proof of a healing mechanism.

note: Preclinical-methodology review mentioning several biofield modalities. Useful for experimental-design/citation context, not independent empirical replication; reproducibility and mechanism acknowledged as unresolved.

note: HIV antiretroviral-regimen claims study; Bengston is an author surname. No Bengston Healing Method intervention.

note: Perforator/propeller flap surgical biogeometry; no named BioGeometry healing intervention. Title establishes surgical topic, abstract unavailable.

title: Inhaled Corticosteroid-Containing Treatment Escalation and Outcomes for Patients with Asthma in a U.S. Health Care Organization.
note: Inhaled-corticosteroid escalation claims study; Bengston is an author surname, not a healing method.

title: The Effects of Meditation on Twin Hearts on P300 Values: A Repeated Measures Comparison of Nonmeditators and the Experienced.
note: 12 experienced Twin Hearts meditators versus 12 nonmeditators, repeated pre/post auditory P300 measures. Selected EEG changes reported; cross-sectional experience and no matched sham limit causation. Surrogate processing measures do not validate PH recipient treatment.

title: Meditation-induced psychosis: a narrative review and individual patient data analysis.
note: Narrative review of 28 reported psychosis cases across varied meditations including PH. Case associations and precipitating factors do not prove causation or estimate incidence; retain adverse-event context without assigning all cases to PH.

title: Age estimation of individuals aged 5-23 years based on dental development of the Indonesian population.
note: Dental development atlas using a modified Bengston eruption system; no Bengston healing intervention.

title: Patient Reported Outcomes of Scalp and Forehead Reconstruction for Defects Following Oncological Resections (North-East Indian Tertiary Cancer Centre Study).
note: Scalp/forehead oncological surgical reconstruction outcomes using tissue bio-geometry. Not BioGeometry energy treatment.

title: Understanding Pranic Energy Experiences: A Qualitative Approach.
note: 100 participants' hand-sensitization reports from 2014, retrospective qualitative analysis explicitly using Master Choa Kok Sui practice. Sensation themes do not objectively demonstrate prana detection or controlled treatment benefit.

title: Differential In Vivo Effects on Cancer Models by Recorded Magnetic Signals Derived From a Healing Technique.
note: Recorded Bengston signals four hours daily approximately one month in three mouse cancer models. Breast-tumor effect reported, melanoma largely null, bladder tumors failed to develop. Sample/room confounding/full bias review pending; no human anticancer efficacy established.

title: Perception of Subtle Energy "Prana", and Its Effects During Biofield Practices: A Qualitative Meta-Synthesis.
note: Qualitative meta-synthesis of 19 heterogeneous prana/biofield perception studies. Describes felt experiences; no objective energy validation or independent clinical replication.

title: The social consequence of wellness: a view of healing outcomes from micro and macro perspectives.
note: Mexican Spiritualist ethnography analyzes individual/social outcomes. No controlled efficacy comparison; distinguish cultural system from other Spiritualist lineages.

title: Utility of Keystone Flap in Armory of Dermatosurgeons.
note: Keystone surgical flap reconstruction with anatomical bio-geometry; no named BioGeometry energy treatment.

title: Ralph G. Bengston.
note: Historical biography of Ralph G. Bengston, no abstract or Bengston Healing Method experiment.

title: Non-medical treatments and their outcomes.
note: Follow-up observations at a Mexican Spiritualist temple report more failures than successes and describe symbolic/tactile practices. No comparator or effect counts in abstract; cultural specificity limits transfer to other Spiritualist lineages.

title: The Effects of Therapeutic Touch on Test Anxiety among Nursing Students: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
note: 46 students, 23/23, randomizer-generated allocation; no sham or participant masking. Baseline anxiety 58.91 versus 40.26; post 25.60 versus 47.43. ANCOVA eta squared .771, but baseline imbalance/expectations and unblinded self-report create substantial bias concern. Procedure: seated, head-to-foot rhythmic scanning approximately 5 cm away, reassess/rebalance, twenty minutes, then rest; no grades measured. Authors report no conflicts or financial support.

title: EFFECT OF THERAPEUTIC TOUCH ON PAIN RELATED PARAMETERS IN PATIENTS WITH CANCER: A RANDOMIZED CLINICAL TRIAL.
note: 90 male cancer patients, 30/30/30 TT/placebo/usual care, convenience recruitment. Allocation method/concealment and assessor masking not described. Seven ten-to-fifteen-minute sessions every three days: deep breathing, scan 5-10 cm away, head-to-foot cleansing and individualized transfer; sham unordered gestures. Selected pain-interference comparisons favored TT. Many endpoints, no extracted confidence intervals and absent rigorous adverse-event ascertainment preclude broad safety claims; IRCT201412094115N3 not independently matched. Authors declare no conflict.

title: Radiation response of cultured human cells is unaffected by Johrei.
note: Four control/four Johrei experiments, 800/856 observed glial cells, four X-ray doses. Randomized wells and scientists blinded. Thirty-minute raised-hand intention at least 20 cm away after four-hour baseline; observation 22.5 hours. Division p=.560 and death p=.456 null; dose significant. Experiment, not individual cell, is replication unit. Funding Center for Science of Life/NCCAM; no patient radiation-protection efficacy established.

title: In vitro test of external Qigong.
note: Three astrocyte colony-formation studies: four pilot, fourteen formal and thirty replication Qigong/sham comparisons, each with equal numbers of systematic negative-control comparisons. Cell plates/locations randomized, coded counting/analysis blinded. Formal sham always first; replication order randomized with temperature logging. Twenty-minute treatment at least 10 cm away; no reproducible effect, pooled result nonsignificant. Environmental variability and absent present-but-not-treating practitioner control limit mechanism inference. NCCAM/Noetic Sciences/Fetzer support reported.

title: Efficacy of Transcendental Meditation to Reduce Stress Among Health Care Workers: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
note: 80 randomized, 78 at three months, open-label TM versus wellness resources. Computer stratification by age/sex through protected REDCap module. Five instructional days then twenty minutes twice daily and three follow-ups. Primary GSI difference -1.8, CI -4.2 to .6, p=.13 nonsignificant; selected secondary burnout/anxiety positive, no multiplicity adjustment. One-month surveys missing for 12/20 participants due to app error. No reported adverse events; expectancy and secondary-outcome testing constrain interpretation.
